newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita to launch DVD player on global market. [CORRECTED 09:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Matsushita to launch DVD player on global market. [CORRECTED 09:25 GMT]

text.p: Japanese consumer electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Monday it plans to start the first sales of digital video disc (DVD) players outside of Japan later this month.
A company spokeswoman said Matsushita would begin the sales in Asia in time for the Chinese New Year shopping season.
Industry analysts said the sales would be the first outside of Japan, where Matsushita started selling DVD players in November, one of the first Japanese makers to do so.

The firm plans to start selling DVD players in Germany on February 1 and in the United States on March 1. The launch in the rest of Europe would be some time after that in Germany, the spokeswoman said.
Matsushita aims to capture a more than 30 percent market share of the total global DVD player market, which it forecasts at two million units in 1997.

A DVD looks like a compact disc (CD) but stores far more information, allowing its to hold feature-length movies, as well as music and other information. Industry experts expect the system to eventually replace video movies, CDs and CD-ROMs.
Toshiba Corp said on Monday it would start selling DVD players in the United States in March, in Asia after the spring and in Europe after the autumn.
(Corrects timing of Toshiba's planned launch in Asia)
Hitachi Ltd said it had not decided overseas launch dates.

Sony Corp said earlier this month it would start selling DVD players in the United States in April and in Europe in mid-1997. The players will be introduced to the rest of Asia, except Japan, after going on sale in the United States.
Toshiba and Hitachi already sell DVD players in Japan. Sony plans to launch its version on the domestic market in March.
The Matsushita spokeswoman said the player that would go on sale in January in Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan and Thailand was a high-grade version, the DVD-A300.
Its features include remote control and karaoke functions and it will cost around 90,000 yen ($769).
The spokeswoman did not give specific launch dates for each Asian market.
All Asian markets have large Chinese communities which celebrate lunar new year, which this year falls on February 7.
In the United States, Matsushita plans to sell two DVD player models, the DVD-A100 and the DVD-A300, at suggested retail prices of $599.95 and $749.95, the spokeswoman said. ($1=117 yen)
